title: HTTPS / DNS C2
overview: Explore repeated DNS lookups classified as high entropy for an uncommon destination domain.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and network sensor or waf projection fields.

attack.name: DNS
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: Three distinct observations of high-entropy labels targeting a rare domain justify a DNS activity pivot.
evidence: Check the DNS host, domain and timestamps, then compare process and egress telemetry for the same host.
false_positive: CDNs, update networks and security agents can emit opaque DNS labels.
tuning: Segment expected infrastructure, track observed domain age externally if available, and check process baselines.
response: Preserve DNS and resolver logs, correlate endpoint process evidence and constrain egress if justified.
prevention: Use controlled resolvers, egress filtering and DNS analytics with reviewed allowlists.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture supplies entropy and rarity classes. The rule does not infer true DNS tunneling or analyze HTTPS content.

options: Endpoint process and egress telemetry for the host
questions.explanation: DNS alone gives network context, while endpoint evidence can identify the requester.

options: Legitimate services can use opaque labels
questions.explanation: Opaque DNS alone can be noisy.
